# p10k-rs v0.1.3

A combined supply-chain + shell-integration release. v0.1.2 hardened
the IPC and render paths. v0.1.3 hardens the **release pipeline**
(every artifact is now signed with sigstore + attested with SLSA
build provenance), wires **OSC 133 semantic prompts** into every
modern terminal, and lands a long tail of fixes across the prompt
UX, config loader, and runtime detection.

**This is the first signed release.** See "How to verify" below for
the user-facing recipe.

30 slices landed across Tier 0 (security patch) and Tier 1 (feature
sprint) waves. 5 items were deliberately deferred to v0.2 — see
"Deferred" at the end.

## What you'll notice (visible changes)

### Modern-terminal shell integration, default on

OSC 133 semantic prompts (`A` / `B` / `C` / `D`) now emit
unconditionally on terminals that benefit — Ghostty, WezTerm, iTerm2,
Kitty, VS Code, Windows Terminal, and any host that exports
`$TERM_PROGRAM`, `$WT_SESSION`, `$GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR`,
`$KITTY_WINDOW_ID`, or an AI-agent env var. Suppressed on Warp
(its block model conflicts).

Configurable via `[shell_integration] mode = "auto" | "always" | "off"`
in `~/.config/p10k-rs/config.toml`. Default: `auto`.

What you get when your terminal supports it:
- `Cmd+Shift+↑`/`Cmd+Shift+↓` to navigate between commands
- Right-click "Copy command output" in supporting hosts
- AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Goose) can identify
  prompt vs. command vs. output boundaries precisely

### Synchronized output

The two-line prompt no longer tears on terminals that support
DECSET 2026. Wraps the render in `\e[?2026h` … `\e[?2026l` with a
Drop guard so a panic still emits the close sequence.

### `p10k-rs config check`

New subcommand validates your TOML config without restarting the
shell. Exit code 0 on success, non-zero with errors on stderr.

### Improved AI-agent detection

Adds generic `AGENT=<name>` and `AI_AGENT=<name>` probes (emerging
cross-tool convention) plus explicit Goose detection. Existing
per-tool probes (Claude Code, Aider, Cursor) keep precedence.

### Small but real polish

- Transient prompt no longer leaves `RPROMPT` artifacts in scrollback
- Bracketed-paste auto-re-arms in `precmd` (defends against output
  that disables it)
- `instant-prompt` dump writes are atomic with 0600 perms
- Sources of the dump file are mode-checked and refused if foreign
- `install.sh` no longer probes the maintainer's dev-machine path

## What you won't notice (but matters)

### Signed releases (the headline)

The release pipeline now ships:

- **`.cosign.bundle` sigstore signature** per tarball — keyless OIDC,
  identity bound to this workflow file + tag, recorded in Rekor.
- **SLSA build-provenance attestation** for the binary and the
  tarball, queryable via `gh attestation verify`.
- Third-party GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs; Dependabot
  auto-bumps weekly with grouped patch+minor PRs.
- Release-tag pattern tightened to `v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*` so
  non-semver pushes don't accidentally release.
- `concurrency: release-${ref}` with `cancel-in-progress: false`
  so partial publishes finish cleanly.

Once signed git tags land (T2.24 in v0.2), this combination meets
**SLSA L3** per slsa.dev/spec/v1.0.

### Filesystem & IPC hardening

- **`git status` shell-out times out at 2 s.** A hostile `.git/`
  (fsmonitor exploit, hung helper) can no longer hang the prompt.
- **`gitstatusd` response cap 1 MiB → 64 KiB.** Defense in depth.
- **`gitstatusd` binary ownership checked.** Refuses to spawn a
  helper owned by neither the current user nor root.
- **Resource caps on `gitstatusd` spawn** (`ulimit -v 524288 -t 30`
  on Linux; CPU-only on macOS where `-v` isn't supported).
- **Config TOML mode + ownership checked.** World/group-writable
  configs are refused with a one-time stderr warning; falls back
  to factory default.
- **Diagnostics log** at `$XDG_STATE_HOME/p10k-rs/diagnostics.log`
  (mode 0600, daily rotation). Binary stderr routes there instead
  of `/dev/null`. Filter via `P10K_RS_LOG=warn` (default).
- **`open_owned_safely` helper** in `p10k-rs-core::safety` —
  O_NOFOLLOW + fstat ownership check, reusable across callers.

### Render-path injection (another layer)

- **`$`, `` ` ``, `\` now escaped in zsh prompt text content**
  (mirroring existing `%` doubling). Closes residual RCE risk
  on unpatched zsh (pre-5.8.1, CVE-2021-45444).
- See `SECURITY.md` for the full threat model.

### Git-as-attacker-input

- **Defensive env on every `git status` spawn:**
  `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=""`, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`,
  `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.
- **`install.sh` requires git ≥ 2.35.2** (CVE-2022-24765 floor).
  Override via `P10K_RS_SKIP_GIT_VERSION_CHECK=1`.

### Bootstrap

- **`get.sh` defaults to the latest tagged release**, not `main`.
  The `curl | bash` flow no longer pulls untagged code. Opt in
  to main via `P10K_RS_REF=main`; pin a tag via
  `P10K_RS_REF=v0.1.3`.

## How to verify this release

Two independent paths. Either is sufficient.

**sigstore signature** (Rekor transparency-log backed):

```bash
cosign verify-blob \
  --bundle p10k-rs-0.1.3-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz.cosign.bundle \
  --certificate-identity-regexp \
    'https://github.com/scurran1986/powerlevel10k-rs/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v.+' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com' \
  p10k-rs-0.1.3-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
```

**SLSA build provenance** (GitHub-native, no extra tooling):

```bash
gh attestation verify p10k-rs-0.1.3-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz \
  --repo scurran1986/powerlevel10k-rs
```

Either proves the artifact was built by this workflow at this tag.
See `SECURITY.md` for the full reporting channel + threat model.

## Build

```bash
cargo build --workspace --locked
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --locked
```

## Deferred to v0.2

Tracked, not abandoned:

- **T0.5** — sha256-pin gitstatusd binary (its own release per roadmap)
- **T1.8** — Transient prompt modes (`off|always|same-dir|unique`)
- **T1.10** — Unicode-class hardening (BiDi/ZWJ/NFC, length cap)
- **T1.11** — Type-system end-to-end `SafeText` for env-driven
  segments (depends on T1.10)
- **T1.24** — 24-bit truecolor + hex/CSS-name TOML schema

See the planning roadmap's "Sprint v0.1 close-out" section for the
deferral rationale.
